questions.question: An exploded diagram draws:
options: The object burst gently apart at its joints, each part floating where it belongs, with lines tracing each fitting to its hole
The object after it has collapsed
Only the warnings for the build
The box the kit arrived in

questions.question: A crossed-out mallet on the instruction sheet commands:
options: Use a mallet for this step

questions.question: The cupboard's side panels carry the letters L and R because:
options: They show which panel is heavier
The panels look like twins but are drilled as mirror images — swapping them turns the shelf-peg holes toward the room

questions.question: Good instructions ask to be read:
options: Once, during the build, at speed
Twice — completely before starting, then step by step with the parts in hand

subtopics.title: The Parts List and the Count Before Building

questions.question: The parts audit comes before the build because:
options: A shortage found now costs a phone call; found at step 10 it costs the afternoon and possibly some unbuilding
The list must be posted back

questions.question: The box holds 9 cam locks against a listed 12, and each shelf needs 4. The full answer is:
options: Three missing; nothing at all can proceed
Three missing; two shelves can be fully secured while the third waits
One missing; every shelf can still be locked

questions.question: Twelve cam locks for shelves needing exactly twelve means:
options: Four spares travel in the box
Each shelf can give up a lock
No spares — one lock lost under the couch halts the third shelf

questions.question: Twenty-five learners using 18 screws each, with screws sold in boxes of 40, need:
options: 12 boxes — 450 screws is 11,25 boxes, and eleven boxes leave the class ten screws short

questions.question: Nailing the back panel on before the shelves are in fails because:
options: The back seals the only open face the shelves slide in through
The back panel is only decorative

questions.question: The thin back panel's structural job is:
options: Keeping the corners at ninety degrees — without it the standing carcass leans into a parallelogram

questions.question: South Africa's plug wiring code is:
options: Brown to earth, blue to live, green-and-yellow to neutral
Blue to live on the right, brown to neutral on the left
Brown to live on the right, blue to neutral on the left, green-and-yellow to earth at the top
Any core to any terminal, as long as the grip is tight

questions.question: Swapping brown and blue in the iron's plug is dangerous because:
options: The iron still heats, but the switch now sits on the neutral, leaving the element live when switched off

subtopics.title: Time, Cost and the Do-It-Yourself Decision

questions.question: With the cupboard at R2 499 and delivery at R300, the three options cost:
options: Self R2 799; warehouse assembly R3 249; handyman R3 339
Self R2 499; warehouse R2 949; handyman R3 039
Self R2 799; warehouse R3 339; handyman R3 249

questions.question: The R450 saving from self-assembly carries a risk because:
options: The Allen key is sold separately
Step 8 needs two people, and a split door panel costs R520 plus a three-week wait

questions.question: The assembly service of R450 on the R2 499 cupboard is, as a percentage of the item's price:
Adding a R550 desk lamp to clear the R3 000 free-assembly threshold means the lamp effectively costs:
options: R100 — and whether that is a bargain depends on whether anyone wanted a lamp

questions.question: In the grammar of an instruction sheet, arrows are:
The paired tick-and-cross drawings show:
options: The same part seated rightly and wrongly, the wrong way struck through — your mistake forbidden in advance

questions.question: Swapping the L and R side panels reveals itself at step 7, when:
options: The shelf-peg holes gaze out at the room with nothing for the shelves to grip

subtopics.title: Count Everything Before You Build Anything

questions.question: The roll-call method for the parts list is:
options: Tick each drawn, coded part as it answers the count against the list
Weigh the box against the invoice

questions.question: The ten-minute count is called insurance because:
options: It protects the whole build from stopping halfway over a missing part
It raises the kit's resale value

questions.question: When scaling up to two cupboards, everything doubles except:
options: The Allen key — one serves both builds

subtopics.title: One Step at a Time, and What a Shortcut Costs

questions.question: A wrong-order move is the longest road in the box because:
options: It must be undone in reverse before the build may continue

questions.question: The cord grip must clamp:
options: The thick outer sheath — never the thin cores, which the grip would bite through

questions.question: The swapped-wires fault is called invisible because:
options: The cores are the same colour
The plug sits behind the ironing board
The iron still heats — everything seems fine while the element stays live with the switch off
Only an electrician may open a plug

questions.question: The self-assembly decision should be stated as:
options: The cheapest number wins, no matter what
Always pay for assembly to be safe
A choice with its reason — the R450 saving weighed against the R520 risk and whether four hands are available
